definitions.explanation: The act of putting theoretical knowledge or principles into practical use.

examples.japanese: この{理論|りろん}を{実際|じっさい}に{応用|おうよう}する。
examples.english: I will apply this theory in practice.

examples.japanese: {応用|おうよう}{問題|もんだい}は{基礎|きそ}より{難|むずか}しい。
examples.english: Application problems are harder than basic ones.

examples.japanese: {科学|かがく}の{応用|おうよう}が{社会|しゃかい}を{変|か}えた。
examples.english: The application of science changed society.

notes:
{応用|おうよう} refers to putting theory or knowledge into practical use. Can function as a noun or する verb.

USAGE AS VERB:
{応用|おうよう}する means to apply or put into practice.

COMMON COMPOUNDS:
- {応用|おうよう}{問題|もんだい}: application problem (in exams)
- {応用|おうよう}{科学|かがく}: applied science
- {応用|おうよう}{力|りょく}: practical ability, applied skills
- {応用|おうよう}{編|へん}: advanced/applied section

CONTRAST WITH {基礎|きそ}:
{基礎|きそ} (basics, foundation) vs {応用|おうよう} (application). This pair is common in education and training: {基礎|きそ}{編|へん} → {応用|おうよう}{編|へん}.

RELATED: {実用|じつよう} (practical use) emphasizes everyday utility.
